description: Messaging patterns decomposed. Point-to-point vs pub-sub. Topic partitioning. Consumer groups. Backpressure. Exactly-once via idempotency + offsets. Outbox + transactional events. Specific systems (Kafka, RabbitMQ, NATS, SQS).

sub_mechanisms.name: kafka_topic_partition
sub_mechanisms.definition: Topic = stream. Each topic has N partitions. Partition = ordered log of messages. Producer keys determine partition.
sub_mechanisms.why: Parallelism unit. Ordering within partition guaranteed. Cross-partition no order. Foundation of Kafka scalability.

sub_mechanisms.name: consumer_group
sub_mechanisms.definition: Multiple consumers share work on a topic. Each partition assigned to one consumer in group.
sub_mechanisms.why: Parallel processing. Add consumers up to partition count. Rebalance on consumer add/remove. Standard Kafka pattern.

sub_mechanisms.name: offset_management
sub_mechanisms.definition: Consumer commits offset = position in partition. Restart resumes from committed offset.
sub_mechanisms.why: Decouples consumer crashes from message loss. Commit before or after processing = different semantics (at-most-once vs at-least-once).

sub_mechanisms.name: kafka_exactly_once
sub_mechanisms.definition: Idempotent producer + transactional offsets. Consumer + producer in one transaction.
sub_mechanisms.why: Pure exactly-once impossible globally. Kafka's: 'effectively' exactly-once within Kafka. Cross-system still requires idempotent consumers.

sub_mechanisms.name: rabbitmq_exchange
sub_mechanisms.definition: Producer publishes to exchange; exchange routes to queues based on routing key. Direct, topic, fanout, headers exchanges.
sub_mechanisms.why: AMQP model: decouple producer routing decisions from queue topology. Flexible routing patterns.

sub_mechanisms.name: ack_nack_redelivery
sub_mechanisms.definition: Consumer acks message → broker deletes. Nack or timeout → broker redelivers.
sub_mechanisms.why: RabbitMQ + SQS at-least-once semantic. Standard message broker pattern. Consumers must be idempotent.

sub_mechanisms.name: competing_consumers
sub_mechanisms.definition: Multiple consumers pull from queue. Broker assigns each message to one consumer (vs fanout to all).
sub_mechanisms.why: Work distribution pattern. Add consumers to scale processing. Standard queue model.

sub_mechanisms.name: publish_subscribe_topic
sub_mechanisms.definition: Producer publishes to topic; all subscribers receive copy. Fanout pattern.
sub_mechanisms.why: One event, many consumers. Kafka topics (consumer groups give pub-sub + competing-consumer hybrid). RabbitMQ fanout exchange. SNS.

sub_mechanisms.name: message_ordering_guarantees
sub_mechanisms.why: Global ordering expensive. Per-partition ordering practical: same partition key → ordered. Choose partition key for required ordering.

sub_mechanisms.name: NATS_subject_hierarchy
sub_mechanisms.why: Lightweight (~50 MB binary). Ultra-low latency. Used for IoT, microservices that don't need Kafka's durability.

sub_mechanisms.name: SQS_managed_queue
sub_mechanisms.definition: AWS managed FIFO + standard queues. No infrastructure to run.
sub_mechanisms.why: Serverless messaging. Pay per message. Cost: less throughput than self-hosted Kafka. Standard for AWS-native architectures.

sub_mechanisms.name: stream_processing_kafka_streams
sub_mechanisms.definition: Kafka Streams: process Kafka topics with stateful operations. Joins, aggregations, windowing.
sub_mechanisms.why: Without separate cluster. JVM library. State stored in RocksDB locally + backed by Kafka. Alternative: Flink, Spark Streaming.

derivation_rules.name: kafka_partition_count_limits_parallelism
derivation_rules.why: Each partition → one consumer in group. Adding consumers beyond P leaves them idle. Tune partition count for expected parallelism + overhead trade-off.

derivation_rules.name: consumer_idempotency_required_for_at_least_once
derivation_rules.why: Crash + restart → reprocess after last committed offset. Without idempotency: side effects double. Standard message broker constraint.

derivation_rules.name: kafka_exactly_once_effectively_via_idempotent_producer_transactional_consumer
if: producer is idempotent + consumer commits offsets transactionally
then: end-to-end semantics within Kafka are effectively exactly-once
derivation_rules.why: Idempotent producer: dedupes producer retries via sequence numbers. Transactional consumer: offset commit + downstream produce atomic. Across Kafka: exactly-once. Beyond Kafka: still need idempotency.

derivation_rules.name: partition_key_determines_ordering_scope
if: messages with same key go to same partition
derivation_rules.why: Order user-id 12345's events → key = user_id → same partition → ordered. Cross-key no order. Pick key for required ordering granularity. Critical Kafka design decision.

derivation_rules.name: managed_queue_simpler_self_hosted_cheaper_at_scale
derivation_rules.why: SQS: pay per request. At millions/sec: SQS bill huge. Kafka: cluster cost amortised. Crossover ~10K msg/sec usually. SQS simpler operationally; Kafka cheaper at scale.
